purpose: Docket PR1: the foundations and domain core of a document filing engine. A document arrives, Docket works out which real record it belongs to, files it to storage and records every step; uncertain matches go to human review instead of being guessed. This PR delivers everything except the durable workflow, API and UI: the project scaffold, local services, the ledger schema, the model gateway, a synthetic test corpus, text extraction, the candidate ladder, corroboration scoring, idempotent storage, the ledger, and a `docket score` command.
mechanism:
1. compose.yaml runs Postgres, the Temporal dev server and SeaweedFS (S3-compatible storage), every published port bound to 127.0.0.1. Alembic migrations (migrations/) create documents, document_sources, events (idempotent on idem_key), filed_documents and budget_ledger.
2. config/records.csv lists about 200 synthetic property units (record id UNIT-####, address, building, current and former tenants, aliases; tenant names unique per unit). config/categories.yaml lists document categories. config/scoring.json holds signal weights and tier thresholds, marked untuned.
3. `docket corpus generate --seed N` (docket/corpus.py) writes a deterministic set of synthetic PDFs plus gold labels covering clean, single-signal, conflict, decoy, injection, duplicate and poison (empty text, corrupt, encrypted, zero-byte, non-PDF, very long) cases. Seeds 7 and 11 are committed.
4. docket/core/extraction.py reads PDF text with pypdf and returns typed results; unreadable inputs become typed rejections (e.g. corrupt, encrypted, no_text_layer).
5. docket/core/candidates.py builds a shortlist of real records: explicit record id (body, subject, filename), normalized address with unit tokens that keep letters, and tenant and former-tenant names, with per-signal strengths; a conflict flag goes up when evidence points to two different records. Building evidence taken from the matched address does not count as a separate signal.
6. docket/core/scoring.py combines signals into a score in [0,1] with tiers (none, medium, strong). Strong needs at least two independent signals; an explicit id alone is never strong; a conflict always forces review; filing requires the strong tier.
7. docket/core/storage.py stores files in S3 with put_if_absent: same key and hash is a no-op, same key with a different hash is a typed error. Keys are built only from config and record values checked against [A-Za-z0-9_-]+.
8. docket/core/ledger.py appends events idempotently and moves document status only along a whitelist; terminal statuses never change.
9. docket/llm/ is the model gateway: OpenRouter through LangChain with structured output, replay (record | replay | live; record refuses non-corpus sources), cost metering, a per-call worst-case budget pre-check and a persisted daily cap; SDK output failures become a non-retryable ParseError. `docket spike-models` checks enum schema compliance (pending: no key).
10. `docket score <pdf>` runs extraction, shortlist and scoring with no model call and prints candidates, signals, score, tier and whether it would auto-file.
11. verify.sh runs ruff, pyright (strict on docket/core), pytest with zero skips, per-module branch coverage (scripts/check_coverage.py) and detect-secrets.
decisions:
- The model may only choose among real candidate records (enforced in a later PR); the deterministic ladder and scoring decide whether anything files.
- Two independent signals are required for a strong match, so injected text with a real record id cannot auto-file on its own.
- Content-addressed, idempotent storage so retries never double-write.
- Status whitelist plus idempotent events so every document ends with one terminal status and a reason.
- S3-compatible SeaweedFS instead of MinIO because MinIO images were unavailable; boto3 stays the client.
- Local services bind to localhost only.
- Rejected: trusting a single explicit id; mocking S3 in storage tests.
readers: README.md → people trying or evaluating the project (recruiters, developers who clone it); docs/adr/ → engineers who want the reasoning; code comments and docstrings → the next maintainer. Cristian's rule for all of them: every comment, description and doc line deliberate, plain short sentences, terms defined on first use, no jargon-heavy decision prose.
